title: Graphing an Upward-Shifted Reciprocal Hyperbola
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y = 1/x + 2 by identifying its parent function, shift, asymptotes, domain, range, and intercepts.

steps.title: Identify the Parent Function and Vertical Shift
steps.explanation: Adding 2 to the parent reciprocal function y = 1/x shifts its graph 2 units upward.
steps.why: Adding a positive constant k = 2 translates the graph vertically upward by 2 units.

steps.title: Determine the Asymptotes, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: The vertical asymptote remains x = 0, and the horizontal asymptote shifts upward from y = 0 to y = 2.
steps.why: Since 1/x is never 0, 1/x + 2 takes every real value except 2.

steps.title: Find the x-Intercept and Key Points
steps.explanation: The left branch passes through (-1, 1) and crosses the x-axis at (-1/2, 0), while the right branch lies above y = 2 and passes through (1, 3).
steps.why: Solving 1/x = -2 yields the unique x-intercept at x = -1/2.
